snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹40 lakh–1.5 crore for a licensed unit with blast freezer and cold room
snapshot.margin_d2c: 50–60% on direct orders, before cold delivery
snapshot.margin_production: 35–45% when you supply cafés, caterers and distributors
snapshot.distribution_note: Every step needs a freezer: your unit, the vehicle, the shop

tailwinds: Quick-commerce dark stores stock frozen snacks in most metros and some tier-2 cities, so a new brand can get freezer space faster than in kirana stores.
Cafés, hostels, caterers and cloud kitchens buy ready momos, parathas and snacks to save on skilled kitchen staff.
Working households are replacing some home cooking with ready-to-cook food.
PMFME gives a capital subsidy to micro food-processing units, which reduces the cost of freezers and machines.
headwinds: Cold-chain logistics costs two to three times more than regular delivery, and one broken link spoils a batch.
Retail freezer space is limited and often goes to the big brands that pay for placement.
Large players and private labels compete on price in the most popular products.
A commercial food-processing setup needs an FSSAI licence, fire safety and a proper cold room, which is a big jump from a home kitchen.
angle_2026: Quick commerce changed the entry route. A small frozen-food brand can now get shelf space in dark stores within weeks instead of fighting for kirana freezers. The catch: they expect steady supply, consistent quality and 25–35% margin, so the brands that last usually build volume with cafés and caterers first.
cost_basis: Estimated for a small unit in a rented space supplying one city, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: Registration or state licence, shelf-life and microbial tests
Steamers, dough mixer, work tables, weighing and sealing machines
Deep freezers at the small end; a blast freezer as you grow
Food-grade pouches or trays, printed cartons, labels
Insulated boxes and gel packs, or a rented refrigerated van
A small commercial kitchen with drainage and power backup
Raw material, salaries and 30–60 days of unpaid B2B invoices

rows: Packaging and cold delivery per pack
unit_economics.note: Supplying cafés in bulk earns less per piece but costs far less to deliver, which is why many frozen-food founders start B2B.

investor_probes: What does cold chain cost per unit, and who pays when a delivery thaws?
How much of revenue comes from B2B customers versus retail, and which one is profitable?
What is your production capacity per day, and what is it running at now?
What is the real shelf life once the pack leaves your freezer?
Why won't a bigger brand or a private label match your product at a lower price?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start by supplying 10–20 cafés, hostels and caterers who order every week and pay within 15 days. That steady volume justifies a blast freezer and FSSAI licence before you chase retail shelves.
sourcing_edge: Buy flour, vegetables and meat from wholesale mandis. The bigger saving is location: set up close to your buyers, because cold transport costs more than most ingredients.
licences: FSSAI registration (turnover under ₹12 lakh) or state licence for a manufacturing unit
Trade licence from your municipality and fire safety clearance for a commercial unit
Legal Metrology declarations on retail packs

hard_truths.title: The cold-chain leak
hard_truths.text: A single power cut, a late van or a shop that switches off its freezer at night can thaw a whole delivery. Refrozen products lose texture and get returned. Budget for losses and insist on temperature logs from partners.

hard_truths.title: The payment cycle
hard_truths.text: Distributors and modern retail often pay in 45–90 days, while you pay for flour and meat in cash. Growing retail sales can drain your bank account faster than slow sales.

hard_truths.title: Freezer space politics
hard_truths.text: Retail freezers are small and crowded. Stores prefer brands that pay for placement, fill gaps reliably and don't need chasing. A missed restock can lose you the slot.

hard_truths.title: The scale bottleneck
hard_truths.text: Moving from a home or shared kitchen to a licensed unit with a blast freezer and cold room is a jump of ₹20–50 lakh. Plan that step with a PMFME or PMEGP loan well before you run out of capacity.

plan_goal: The aim is ₹1 lakh in sales, mostly from repeat B2B orders, before you invest in a larger unit.

plan.title: Validate and source
steps: Cook three versions of your hero product and test them with 30 target customers and 5 café owners.
Freeze samples for two weeks and check taste and texture after reheating.
Get quotes for ingredients, packaging and a deep freezer.

plan.title: Compliance and pilot batch
steps: Get FSSAI, Udyam and GST registration.
Produce a pilot run of 200–300 packs with proper labels and batch codes.
Set up cold delivery for a 5 km radius.

plan.title: Sell directly
steps: Offer free trial packs to 20 cafés, hostels and caterers; convert them to weekly orders.
Sell to households through apartment WhatsApp groups and a weekend stall.
Track reorders and complaints for every customer.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Calculate the real cost per pack, including wastage and delivery.
Check how quickly B2B customers pay.
Decide whether to approach quick commerce or add capacity first.
